adoptionRule: One vocabulary for the whole S1 slice: the synthetic values of tests/bdd/features/live-model-choice*.feature. Values are fixed before implementation and are not read from implementation code or the system under test. Editable only together with design.md before the contract is adopted.
identityNote: BDD runs use the deployment's auth-off test configuration (tests/bdd/playwright.config.ts) and send no credentials; the operator is the deployment's own authority. No external identity proxy is involved.

timeComparator.display: HH:MM:SS in the browser's time zone
timeComparator.rule: the receipt's change time lies inside [t0 - 2 s, t1 + 2 s] where t0 is the harness clock before the operator's confirm click and t1 the harness clock when the live route acknowledged; it must NOT lie inside the window of any other change; consecutive default changes are at least 5 seconds apart (step: 5 seconds have passed since the system default was set)
timeComparator.truthSource: harness clock (browser and server share one host); the store read-back of the default row's update time is a second truth when its route is named (UNVERIFIED)

confirmationComparator.mechanism: the harness intercepts POST /api/uar/providers/bdd-provider-b/default with Playwright page.route and holds it; the PUT before it is not held
assertionsWhileHeld: the system-default control does not show bdd-provider-b/claude-5-haiku as the live pair and still shows openai/gpt-5.4-mini
a registry read-back (GET /api/uar/providers, not the UI) still returns default_id openai
confirmationComparator.assertionAfterRelease: after route.continue() lets the server answer, a confirmation appears showing the requested value bdd-provider-b/claude-5-haiku and the activation `live`, and the control shows the new live pair
confirmationComparator.rejects: an optimistic UI that shows the confirmation or the new pair on click, before the live route answers (the baseline's optimisticUpsert, frontend/src/features/providers/model/providers-store.ts:156-176); also a UI that confirms after the PUT returns but before, or without, the POST; and a UI that sends the POST but confirms without awaiting its answer (caught by the polled hold window)
confirmationComparator.heldArrivalCondition: the step attaches a page response listener that records the status of PUT /api/uar/providers/bdd-provider-b and arms page.route on POST /api/uar/providers/*/default, both before the confirm click; it waits until the route handler has signalled that a POST was intercepted whose URL path is exactly /api/uar/providers/bdd-provider-b/default (the live route carries no body) and the recorded PUT status is 2xx; it then keeps the POST held for holdWindowMs (2000 ms), polling at most every 100 ms that no confirmation element is visible (any appearance fails the step), and returns at the end of that window; the step never waits for a response to the held POST
confirmationComparator.assertionsTiming: assertionsWhileHeld run after the held step returns, at the end of the 2000 ms hold and immediately before release; a confirmation that appears at any time during the hold fails the scenario, so a console that confirms after sending the POST without awaiting its answer is rejected

heldRouteControl.scenario: A default change whose acknowledgement fails shows no confirmation
heldRouteControl.mechanism: the held POST is fulfilled with status 500 (route.fulfill); later matching requests are passed through to the server so a retry or second POST would change the registry

expected.errorShown: a visible error that says the system default was not changed

noFurtherWrite.rule: the browser issues no write request to /api/uar/** in the window (the one PUT already made is excluded)

heldRouteControl.rejects: a UI that confirms or flips the control before the route answers, or that swallows the failure
heldRouteControl.guards: a console that, after the 500, falls back to another write path that reaches the server: a second POST to the default route (passed through once the first is fulfilled) or a PUT of llm.default_provider; and a UI that confirms or flips the control anyway
heldRouteControl.notClaimed: the held request never reaches the server, so the registry read-back cannot detect the 500 itself; it only detects a fallback write that does reach the server

samples.stoppingRule: fixed N=3 with --repeat-each=3 --retries=0, every sample must pass

mutants.rule: A mutant is the candidate commit named in the implementation-complete inventory plus exactly one patch file. The patch's sha256 is recorded in the inventory; the run refuses to start if the digest differs, or if `git diff --name-only <candidate>..` on the mutant tree lists any file other than the patch's single target. Judgement is made from the mutant's JSON reporter file, never from the exit status. A failure at any other step is control INVALID, not a pass.
